name: Connecticut
modelName: Income shares, combined net weekly income schedule (Regs. Conn. State Agencies § 46b-215a-2c)
incomeDefinition: Gross income (wages, overtime and second jobs up to 45 paid hours per week, self-employment, benefits, etc.; § 46b-215a-1(11)) minus allowable deductions: federal, state and local income tax, Social Security or mandatory retirement, Medicare tax, CT FMLI contributions, health insurance premiums for the parent and dependents, court-ordered life and disability insurance, mandatory union dues, mandatory uniforms and tools, alimony and child support ordered for others, and the qualified child deduction (§ 46b-215a-2c(c)(2), § 46b-215a-2c(d)).

schedule.columns: combined net weekly income, then obligation for 1..6 children, then the schedule percentage for 1..6 children
schedule.lookupRule: Round the combined net weekly income (or, for a low-income obligor, the noncustodial parent's income) to the nearest ten dollars and read the block for the number of children (§ 46b-215a-2c(c)(3)(A)-(B)). Each parent's share = own net income / combined, rounded to the nearest whole percentage, x the obligation (§ 46b-215a-2c(c)(4)).

belowMin.rule: The schedule starts at $150 net weekly income (the minimum income triggering an obligation was raised from $50 to $150, preamble (b)(2)(B)). In the darker shaded area (noncustodial parent net weekly income up to $470 for 1 child, $550 for 2, $610 for 3, $680 for 4, $750 for 5, $830 for 6) the noncustodial parent is a low-income obligor and the block amount based on that parent's own income alone is the basic obligation (§ 46b-215a-1(16), § 46b-215a-2c(c)(3)(A)(i)).

aboveMax.text: Above $6,000 combined net weekly income, awards are set case by case: the amount at $6,000 is the minimum presumptive obligation and the maximum is combined net weekly income x the percentage shown at $6,000 (12.61%, 18.27%, 20.97%, 23.42%, 25.77%, 28.01% for 1-6 children) (§ 46b-215a-2c(a)(2)).

formula.text: Income rounded to the nearest ten dollars and percentage shares rounded to the nearest whole percentage (Regs. Conn. State Agencies § 46b-215a-2c(c)(3)-(4)); orders rounded to the nearest dollar (§ 46b-215a-2c(c)(6)(A)); above $6,000 the amount at $6,000 is the minimum and the percentage at $6,000 x income the maximum (§ 46b-215a-2c(a)(2)).

shared.text: No time-based formula. In shared physical custody (substantially equal time; exact equality not required, § 46b-215a-1(24)) the presumptive order is the presumptive current support amount of the parent with the higher net weekly income, payable to the lower-income parent (§ 46b-215a-2c(c)(7)(B)); a deviation may apply if the arrangement substantially reduces/increases expenses or incomes are substantially equal (§ 46b-215a-5c(b)(6)(A)). Split custody: offset of the two theoretical amounts (§ 46b-215a-2c(c)(7)(A)).

addOns.childcare: Qualifying child care costs (employment-related, licensed source) are shared by the noncustodial parent's percentage share of combined net disposable income; low-income obligors pay a reduced share (e.g. 20% of costs when the custodial parent's income is outside the shaded area) (§ 46b-215a-2c(g)).
addOns.healthInsurance: Each award must include health care coverage: insurance at reasonable cost, application for HUSKY B, and/or cash medical support; no HUSKY contribution may be ordered from a low-income obligor (§ 46b-215a-2c(f)).
addOns.text: Health care coverage and child care contribution are separate award components added to current support (§ 46b-215a-2c(a)(1), (f), (g)).

lowIncome.rule: The schedule's darker shaded low-income area is based on a self-support reserve of $362 net per week (125% of the 2024 federal poverty guideline for one person, preamble (e)); in that area the obligation uses only the noncustodial parent's income and is 10% of net income for one child below $362, phased out up to $470 (§ 46b-215a-1(16), § 46b-215a-2c(c)(3)(A)). Arrearage payments for a low-income obligor are the greater of 10% of current support or $1 per week (§ 46b-215a-3a).

statute.cite: Conn. Gen. Stat. § 46b-215a; Regs. Conn. State Agencies §§ 46b-215a-1 to 46b-215a-6

emancipation.text: Support runs to 18; an unmarried child who is a full-time high school student is maintained until completing grade 12 or turning 19, whichever is first (Conn. Gen. Stat. § 46b-84(b)); support for a child with a disability may run to 21 (§ 46b-84(c)). Educational support orders for college are possible under § 46b-56c.

testCases.what: noncustodial parent A's presumptive weekly current support
testCases.source: Computed by hand from the official schedule: combined $1,500 -> 2 children $465; A share 1000/1500 rounded to 67% (§ 46b-215a-2c(c)(4)(B)); 0.67 x 465 = 311.55, rounded to $312 (§ 46b-215a-2c(c)(6)(A)).

testCases.what: low-income noncustodial parent A's weekly current support
testCases.source: Computed by hand: A's own $400 falls in the darker shaded area for 1 child (<= $470), so the block amount $61 is the obligation regardless of B's income (§ 46b-215a-2c(c)(3)(A)(i), (c)(4)(A)).

testCases.what: payer A's weekly current support above the schedule (minimum presumptive)
testCases.source: Computed by hand: combined $7,000 > $6,000; minimum presumptive = amount at $6,000 for 2 children ($1,096) x A share 71% = 778.16 -> $778 (§ 46b-215a-2c(a)(2), (c)(4)); the maximum would use 18.27% of $7,000.

facts.text: Connecticut's new guidelines took effect August 1, 2026, replacing the 2015 guidelines; the schedule now runs to $6,000 combined net weekly income (previously $4,000).
Connecticut works in weekly amounts: incomes and orders are entered on the worksheet as weekly figures (§ 46b-215a-2c(b)).

The low-income area is built on a self-support reserve of $362 net per week (125% of the 2024 federal poverty guideline), and the minimum income triggering an obligation rose from $50 to $150 per week (preamble).
Income from hours worked beyond 45 paid hours per week is excluded from gross income (up to 52 hours it may justify a deviation) (§ 46b-215a-1(11), § 46b-215a-5c(b)(1)(E)).
Connecticut rejects a time-sharing formula: shared physical custody is a deviation criterion, not a mathematical adjustment (preamble (j)(3)(D), § 46b-215a-5c(b)(6)(A)).

uncertain: The darker shaded (low-income) area is shown only by shading in the PDF; the per-column limits (470, 550, 610, 680, 750, 830) were detected from the PDF fill colour by script and match the preamble ($470 for one child) and the point where each column's percentage reaches its plateau.
The guidelines booklet was read from the Judicial Branch copy (jud.ct.gov); the eRegulations copy (eregulations.ct.gov) was not checked.
